stem: A retailer is designing a new workload and wants explicit architectural guidance on lowering the energy consumption and environmental impact of the resources it runs. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar addresses that goal?

options.text: Reliability, which covers performing an intended function correctly and consistently
Sustainability, which focuses on environmental impact and energy efficiency
Cost optimization, which covers delivering business value at the lowest price point
Operational excellence, which focuses on building software correctly and delivering a great customer experience

explanation: Sustainability is the Well-Architected pillar defined around environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency as the levers an architect can act on. The other options target workload correctness, spend, and software delivery rather than environmental footprint.

distractorNotes.a: Reliability is about a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, not about energy use.
distractorNotes.c: Cost optimization targets the lowest price point for business value, which is a financial rather than environmental goal.
distractorNotes.d: Operational excellence focuses on building software correctly and delivering a great customer experience, not environmental impact.

sourceNote: Well-Architected Framework - Sustainability pillar definition

stem: During a large migration, one legacy application will move to AWS with no changes made to the application itself. A second application will move to AWS with its self-managed SQL Server database switched to Amazon RDS for SQL Server. Which TWO of the 7 Rs migration strategies do these two plans use? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Retire, which decommissions an application rather than moving it at all
Rehost, also called lift and shift, which moves an application unchanged
Repurchase, which replaces the application with a different product
Replatform, which moves an application and applies some optimization
Refactor, which re-architects an application around cloud-native features

explanation: AWS documents seven migration strategies, the 7 Rs. Rehost is described as lift and shift: the application moves from the source environment to AWS without any changes, which matches the first application. Replatform is described as lift, tinker, and shift: the application moves with some optimization applied, and AWS gives replatforming a SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server as the example, which matches the second application.

distractorNotes.a: Retire applies to applications you decommission or archive instead of migrating.
distractorNotes.c: Repurchase, or drop and shop, means replacing the application with a different product such as a SaaS offering.
distractorNotes.e: Refactor means modifying the architecture to use cloud-native features, which is more than the described change.

sourceNote: AWS Prescriptive Guidance - the 7 Rs migration strategies, rehost and replatform

stem: A company currently buys and racks servers years in advance to cover projected peak demand. After it moves those workloads to AWS, how does its infrastructure spending model primarily change?

options.text: Fixed upfront expense becomes variable expense, paying only for what it uses
The same fixed capital purchase cycle continues, but AWS installs the hardware
One flat annual platform fee is charged that covers unlimited AWS consumption
Infrastructure spending disappears entirely because AWS absorbs the compute cost

explanation: AWS describes trading fixed expense for variable expense as a core advantage of cloud computing: instead of investing heavily in data centers and servers before knowing how they will be used, you pay only when you consume computing resources and only for how much you consume. Capacity no longer has to be bought ahead of demand.

distractorNotes.b: The point of the change is that the upfront capital purchase cycle goes away, not that AWS performs it for you.
distractorNotes.c: AWS consumption is metered per use; there is no flat all-you-can-use annual platform fee.
distractorNotes.d: Spending does not disappear; it shifts from upfront capital purchases to metered consumption charges.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - trade fixed expense for variable expense

stem: A media company cannot predict traffic for an upcoming launch and does not want to buy capacity for a peak that may never happen. Which AWS Well-Architected general design principle does running this workload on AWS let the team apply?

options.text: Improve through game days, by simulating production events on a schedule
Drive architectures using data gathered about how the workload behaves
Stop guessing capacity needs, scaling in and out automatically as required
Test systems at production scale using a full-size environment on demand

explanation: Stop guessing your capacity needs is a general design principle of the Well-Architected Framework. AWS notes that a poor capacity decision leaves you either with expensive idle resources or with the performance consequences of too little capacity, and that in the cloud you can use as much or as little capacity as you need and scale in and out automatically. That directly answers unpredictable launch traffic.

distractorNotes.a: Game days are scheduled simulations of production events to test architecture and processes, not a response to unknown demand.
distractorNotes.b: Driving architectures using data is about collecting evidence to improve design choices over time.
distractorNotes.d: Testing at production scale is about creating and then decommissioning a full-size test environment, not about sizing live capacity.

sourceNote: Well-Architected Framework - general design principle: stop guessing your capacity needs

stem: An enterprise is planning a large-scale migration to the AWS Cloud. The leadership team wants to establish training roadmaps, upskill existing staff on cloud technologies, and adapt its organizational culture and team structures to support the new operating model. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspective primarily addresses these capabilities?

options.text: Business perspective, which focuses on aligning cloud investments with digital transformation ambitions and business outcomes
Platform perspective, which focuses on building an enterprise-grade scalable cloud environment and modernizing workloads
Governance perspective, which focuses on orchestrating cloud initiatives, managing portfolios, and minimizing project risk
People perspective, which focuses on evolving culture, organizational structure, leadership, and workforce development

explanation: The People perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) serves as the bridge between technology and business, focusing on evolving organizational culture, structure, leadership, and workforce capability. It encompasses capabilities such as cloud fluency, workforce upskilling, and organizational change management. The Business, Platform, and Governance perspectives address strategic investment alignment, technical cloud infrastructure, and risk/portfolio governance, respectively.

distractorNotes.a: The Business perspective focuses on ensuring cloud investments align with business outcomes and strategic digital transformation ambitions, not on organizational training or workforce skills.
distractorNotes.b: The Platform perspective focuses on technical architecture, platform engineering, and workload modernization, not on employee upskilling or organizational culture.
distractorNotes.c: The Governance perspective focuses on portfolio management, risk mitigation, and cloud investment orchestration, not on human resources or talent enablement.

sourceNote: AWS CAF - foundational capabilities and six perspectives

stem: A software startup wants to accelerate experimentation by allowing engineering teams to provision and tear down complete development and testing environments in minutes rather than waiting weeks for physical hardware procurement. Which advantage of cloud computing does this improvement primarily reflect?

options.text: Benefiting from massive economies of scale, aggregating usage across customers to lower variable pricing
Increasing speed and agility, reducing resource provisioning time to lower the cost and barrier of experimentation
Achieving high availability, engineering redundant architecture to maintain continuous uptime during outages
Eliminating data center maintenance, removing the physical facility operational burden of server racking and power

explanation: AWS defines increasing speed and agility as a core advantage of cloud computing: because new IT resources are only a click away, the time required to make resources available to developers drops from weeks to minutes. This lowers the cost and time of experimentation, allowing organizations to innovate more rapidly. Economies of scale lower usage prices, high availability ensures fault-tolerant operation, and eliminating data center management removes physical infrastructure overhead.

distractorNotes.a: Massive economies of scale refers to AWS aggregating usage across hundreds of thousands of customers to achieve lower pay-as-you-go pricing, not the speed of developer provisioning.
distractorNotes.c: High availability refers to designing resilient systems that remain accessible and operational through component failures, not reducing provisioning lead times for testing.
distractorNotes.d: Stopping spending money on data centers relieves the burden of facility management and hardware installation, but the rapid on-demand provisioning and testing velocity specifically defines agility.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - increase speed and agility

stem: A ticketing platform experiences sudden, unpredictable surges in user traffic during flash sales that last 20 minutes, followed by an immediate drop to baseline traffic. The company needs infrastructure that automatically provisions capacity during spikes and deprovisions it when traffic subsides to minimize idle resource costs. Which AWS Cloud attribute provides this dynamic behavior?

options.text: Scalability, which accommodates long-term workload growth by continually adding storage and processing capacity
Elasticity, which dynamically acquires and releases computing resources in response to immediate demand changes
Reliability, which ensures that an application recovers consistently from transient network and service disruptions
Agility, which reduces the time required for engineering teams to develop and deploy new software applications

explanation: Elasticity is the ability to dynamically acquire resources when needed and release them when no longer required, matching capacity directly to fluctuating demand and avoiding paying for idle resources. Scalability refers to handling larger workloads over time, reliability focuses on recovering from failures, and agility relates to rapid software development and deployment.

distractorNotes.a: Scalability refers to an architecture's capability to handle increasing workloads over time by expanding capacity, but elasticity specifically describes dynamically scaling in and out in real time.
distractorNotes.c: Reliability focuses on an application's ability to operate consistently and recover from failures, not the dynamic scaling of resources.
distractorNotes.d: Agility describes the speed with which organizations can develop, test, and launch new applications, not automated resource provisioning.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - stop guessing capacity needs

stem: A startup based in Australia wants to expand its streaming service to customers across Europe and North America. The engineering team wants to deliver low-latency playback to international users without purchasing physical servers or negotiating international data center co-location leases. Which advantage of cloud computing does this reflect?

options.text: Massive economies of scale, aggregating worldwide customer usage to negotiate cheaper telecommunication rates
Eliminating data center maintenance, removing routine operating system patching tasks from application developers
Going global in minutes, deploying applications across multiple AWS Regions worldwide to provide lower latency
Trading fixed expense for variable expense, converting annual subscription license fees into metered hourly costs

explanation: AWS defines 'go global in minutes' as a core advantage of cloud computing: organizations can easily deploy applications in multiple AWS Regions around the world with a few clicks, providing lower latency and an improved experience for global customers at minimal cost.

distractorNotes.a: Massive economies of scale refers to AWS achieving higher purchasing power and lower pay-as-you-go prices due to aggregate customer usage, not geographic deployment speed.
distractorNotes.b: Eliminating data center maintenance relieves organizations from physical facility operations, but global multi-region deployment speed specifically defines going global in minutes.
distractorNotes.d: Trading fixed expense for variable expense refers to the financial model shift from upfront capital commitments to consumption billing, not multi-region geographic reach.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - go global in minutes

stem: A financial services application is deployed across multiple Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. If a hardware failure causes an entire Availability Zone to become unavailable, incoming traffic is automatically redirected to healthy instances in the remaining Availability Zones with no service interruption. Which architectural characteristic does this design demonstrate?

options.text: High availability, maintaining uninterrupted operational uptime by eliminating single points of failure
Elasticity, dynamically resizing compute instances in real time to handle fluctuating user request volumes
Agility, accelerating the deployment pipeline so developers can push critical bug fixes to production safely
Economy of scale, pooling compute capacity across multiple accounts to minimize hourly infrastructure bills

explanation: High availability is the characteristic of a system designed to remain accessible and operational without interruption despite component failures, typically achieved by deploying redundant resources across multiple Availability Zones and removing single points of failure. Elasticity is dynamic scaling, agility is speed of innovation, and economies of scale relate to shared cloud purchasing power.

distractorNotes.b: Elasticity describes dynamically growing and shrinking resource capacity in response to fluctuating load, not surviving infrastructure zone failures.
distractorNotes.c: Agility relates to organizational and developer speed in building and shipping software, not architectural fault mitigation.
distractorNotes.d: Economies of scale refers to cost savings derived from AWS's massive customer aggregation, not multi-AZ application resiliency.

sourceNote: Reliability pillar - Availability definition and multi-AZ resilience

stem: A healthcare provider's leadership team wants its technology personnel to stop spending time managing HVAC cooling systems, physical perimeter security, diesel backup generators, and server rack installations, and instead dedicate their time to clinical software innovation. Which AWS Cloud benefit directly addresses this shift?

options.text: Increasing speed and agility, allowing software developers to deploy test environments in minutes
Benefiting from massive economies of scale, lowering per-unit storage costs through pooled purchasing
Trading fixed expense for variable expense, replacing metered utility bills with long-term contracts
Stopping spending money running and maintaining data centers, eliminating physical infrastructure burdens

explanation: AWS defines 'stop spending money running and maintaining data centers' as a primary advantage of cloud computing. By shifting physical infrastructure management—such as power, cooling, real estate, and server racking—to AWS, businesses eliminate undifferentiated heavy lifting and focus resources on projects that differentiate their business.

distractorNotes.a: Increasing speed and agility refers to rapid on-demand provisioning and software deployment speed, not the elimination of physical facilities maintenance.
distractorNotes.b: Massive economies of scale refers to lower usage pricing resulting from AWS's aggregate purchasing power, not the removal of physical data center tasks.
distractorNotes.c: Trading fixed expense for variable expense is a financial cash flow advantage; furthermore, cloud computing replaces upfront capital investments with metered consumption, not the reverse.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - stop spending money running data centers

stem: An organization is building an executive business case to justify migrating its legacy workloads to the AWS Cloud. Which TWO of the following are documented in the AWS Cloud value proposition as core advantages of cloud computing? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Eliminating all operating system patching responsibilities for Amazon EC2 virtual machine instances
Benefiting from massive economies of scale, yielding lower pay-as-you-go prices from aggregate usage
Guaranteeing zero latency for all worldwide network transactions through dedicated physical circuits
Eliminating variable operational expenses by prepaying fixed lifetime hardware maintenance contracts
Stopping guessing capacity needs, scaling dynamically to prevent idle capacity and underprovisioning

explanation: The six advantages of cloud computing documented by AWS include: (1) trade fixed expense for variable expense, (2) benefit from massive economies of scale, (3) stop guessing capacity, (4) increase speed and agility, (5) stop spending money running and maintaining data centers, and (6) go global in minutes. EC2 guest OS patching remains a customer responsibility under the Shared Responsibility Model, zero latency is physically impossible, and cloud computing replaces fixed prepayments with variable expenses.

distractorNotes.a: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, customers remain fully responsible for patching the guest operating system on Amazon EC2 instances.
distractorNotes.c: The cloud provides global infrastructure and low latency, but cannot guarantee zero network latency due to physical limits.
distractorNotes.d: Cloud computing shifts costs from fixed upfront capital investments to variable pay-as-you-go operating expenses, not the reverse.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - economies of scale and capacity

stem: An architecture team wants guidance on designing systems that can automatically recover from infrastructure or service disruptions, dynamically acquire computing resources to meet fluctuating demand, and mitigate disruptions such as misconfigurations or transient network issues. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on these capabilities?

options.text: Reliability, which focuses on performing intended functions correctly and consistently while recovering from failures
Operational excellence, which focuses on running workloads effectively and gaining continuous operational insight
Performance efficiency, which focuses on structured computing resource selection and maintaining high throughput
Cost optimization, which focuses on maximizing business value delivery at the lowest sustainable price point

explanation: The Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework encompasses the ability of a workload to perform its intended function correctly and consistently when expected. This includes the ability to operate and test the workload through its total lifecycle, automatically recover from disruptions, and dynamically allocate compute capacity to meet demand.

distractorNotes.b: Operational excellence focuses on executing operations as code, continuously refining operations procedures, and delivering business value.
distractorNotes.c: Performance efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand changes.
distractorNotes.d: Cost optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary spending and understanding where money is being spent across cloud workloads.

stem: A software engineering department wants to establish operational standards where all infrastructure configurations are defined as code, systems are updated using frequent, small, reversible changes, and operational failures are treated as learning opportunities through structured root-cause analysis. options.text: Security, which focuses on establishing least privilege access and applying multi-layered defense-in-depth
Operational excellence, which focuses on running workloads effectively and continually improving processes
Sustainability, which focuses on minimizing environmental impacts and reducing energy consumption footprints
Performance efficiency, which focuses on adopting serverless architectures to streamline processing throughput

explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving processes and procedures. Its key design principles include: perform operations as code, make frequent, small, reversible changes, refine operations procedures frequently, anticipate failure, and learn from all operational failures.

distractorNotes.a: The Security pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets while delivering business value through risk assessments and mitigation strategies.
distractorNotes.c: The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads, with a primary focus on energy reduction.

Operational excellence, which outlines procedures for automating runbooks and managing daily production releases
Security, which outlines practices for protecting information, user identities, systems, and sensitive assets
Sustainability, which outlines methodologies for reducing carbon emissions and managing compute energy metrics

explanation: The Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets while delivering business value through risk assessments and mitigation strategies. Its foundational design principles include implementing a strong identity foundation, enabling traceability, applying security at all layers, protecting data in transit and at rest, and preparing for security events.

distractorNotes.a: Reliability focuses on workload resiliency, fault tolerance, and automated failure recovery, not confidentiality or data protection.
distractorNotes.b: Operational excellence focuses on process refinement, release automation, and system health observability.

options.text: Cost optimization, which focuses on practicing financial governance and negotiating bulk commitment discounts

Sustainability, which focuses on selecting energy-efficient instance processors to reduce greenhouse emissions

explanation: The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve. Its design principles include: democratize advanced technologies (adopting managed services), go global in minutes, use serverless architectures, experiment more often, and consider mechanical sympathy.

distractorNotes.a: Cost optimization focuses on cloud financial management and eliminating unneeded expenditure, not technology selection for throughput and efficiency.
distractorNotes.b: Operational excellence focuses on operational procedures, runbooks, and continuous process improvements.

distractorNotes.b: The Reliability pillar focuses on workload availability, fault tolerance, and failure recovery.
distractorNotes.c: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on operational runbooks, automation, and ongoing process improvement.

stem: An IT leadership team is establishing enterprise cloud architectural guidelines. Which TWO of the following are recognized general design principles of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Automate to make architectural experimentation easier, creating and replicating systems at minimal cost
Standardize on monolithic application architectures to streamline cross-service logging and monitoring
Drive architectures using data, analyzing telemetry about workload behavior to make empirical decisions
Provision maximum estimated peak capacity upfront to avoid automated resource scaling initialization delays
Transfer all regulatory data governance and security compliance duties entirely to the cloud vendor

explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Framework establishes six general design principles: (1) stop guessing your capacity needs, (2) test systems at production scale, (3) automate to make architectural experimentation easier, (4) allow for evolutionary architectures, (5) drive architectures using data, and (6) improve through game days. Monolithic standardization is not a design principle, overprovisioning violates stopping guessing capacity, and compliance is shared under the Shared Responsibility Model.

distractorNotes.b: AWS encourages loosely coupled, evolutionary architectures rather than standardizing on monolithic application designs.
distractorNotes.d: AWS advocates 'stop guessing your capacity needs' and using elasticity to scale automatically, rather than overprovisioning peak capacity upfront.
distractorNotes.e: Compliance is a shared responsibility between AWS and the customer; customers always retain responsibility for their own data governance.

sourceNote: Well-Architected Framework - general design principles overview

stem: An engineering team is designing a new cloud platform. Rather than making static, one-time technology decisions that lock the business into rigid technical debt, the architects leverage on-demand cloud automation to test, evolve, and swap architectural components incrementally as business requirements change. Which AWS Well-Architected general design principle does this approach implement?

options.text: Improve through game days, scheduling simulated incident exercises to evaluate operational responses
Allow for evolutionary architectures, using automation and on-demand testing to evolve designs safely
Test systems at production scale, duplicating complete production fleets on demand for performance testing
Stop guessing capacity needs, configuring dynamic auto-scaling policies to handle variable daily demand

explanation: Allow for evolutionary architectures is a Well-Architected general design principle. In a traditional environment, architectural decisions are often permanent, one-way doors that result in legacy technical debt. In the cloud, the capability to automate and test on demand lowers the risk of impact from design changes, allowing systems to evolve over time to take advantage of new innovations.

distractorNotes.a: Improve through game days is the design principle of regularly simulating production events to test architectures and operational procedures, not evolving system designs.
distractorNotes.c: Test systems at production scale is the principle of creating full-scale test environments on demand and decommissioning them after testing.
distractorNotes.d: Stop guessing capacity needs focuses on eliminating overprovisioning and underprovisioning through elasticity, not architectural evolution.

sourceNote: Well-Architected Framework - general design principle: allow for evolutionary architectures

stem: Before a major annual promotional event, an e-commerce company wants to test whether its ordering system can process five times normal peak volume. options.text: Improve through game days, simulating production operational outages to test team response runbooks
Drive architectures using data, aggregating metrics from user clickstreams to make caching decisions
Test systems at production scale, creating full-capacity environments on demand for testing and then deleting them
Automate to make architectural experimentation easier, running automated regression scripts across microservices

explanation: Test systems at production scale is a Well-Architected general design principle. In traditional on-premises environments, testing at full production scale is rarely done because of the capital expense of duplicate hardware. In the cloud, you can create a production-scale environment on demand, complete your testing, and then decommission the resources, paying only for the hours consumed.

distractorNotes.a: Game days simulate production operational incidents to validate team procedures and organizational resilience, not full-scale load testing.
distractorNotes.b: Driving architectures using data is about collecting empirical workload telemetry to guide design choices.
distractorNotes.d: Automating experimentation enables rapid replication of architectures to test novel ideas, but testing full-scale production load specifically embodies testing at production scale.

sourceNote: Well-Architected Framework - general design principle: test systems at production scale

stem: An enterprise operates several hundred virtual machines running on an on-premises VMware vSphere infrastructure. The organization wants to move these workloads to AWS quickly without purchasing new hardware, rewriting software, changing existing IP addresses, or converting virtual machine disk formats. Which of the 7 Rs migration strategies does this approach represent?

options.text: Rehost, which involves capturing disk images and recreating instances using standard Amazon EC2 AMIs
Repurchase, which involves dropping custom legacy software and switching to an enterprise SaaS platform
Refactor, which involves redesigning monolithic software components into serverless microservice functions
Relocate, which involves transferring servers to a cloud-based hypervisor platform without format conversion

explanation: Relocate (also called hypervisor-level lift and shift) involves moving servers or workloads to AWS without purchasing new hardware, rewriting software, or modifying existing operations. The classic example documented by AWS is relocating VMware-based virtual machines directly to VMware Cloud on AWS, which avoids virtual machine conversions and preserves IP addressing and configuration.

distractorNotes.a: Rehost (lift and shift) moves applications to Amazon EC2 without changes to the application itself, but does not use hypervisor-level migration (e.g. VMware Cloud on AWS) and typically requires disk format translation.
distractorNotes.b: Repurchase (drop and shop) involves abandoning custom on-premises software and purchasing an off-the-shelf product or SaaS application.
distractorNotes.c: Refactor involves fundamentally re-architecting an application to leverage cloud-native features and serverless services.

sourceNote: AWS Prescriptive Guidance - 7 Rs migration strategies, relocate definition

stem: During a comprehensive cloud migration assessment, an enterprise catalogs its software portfolio. Application 1 has been superseded by an existing internal platform and has no active users. Application 2 is subject to strict national data sovereignty laws that prohibit cloud hosting, so management decides not to move it. Which TWO of the 7 Rs migration strategies describe the dispositions for these applications? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Rehost, transferring the application to Amazon EC2 virtual instances without modifying the codebase
Retire, explicitly decommissioning and shutting down applications that no longer deliver business value
Refactor, re-architecting the application to use cloud-native managed services and container pipelines
Retain, keeping applications in their source environment when migration is blocked or unfeasible
Repurchase, abandoning the proprietary application in favor of an off-the-shelf SaaS alternative

explanation: In the AWS 7 Rs migration framework: Retire means decommissioning or archiving applications that are no longer needed (Application 1). Retain (sometimes called revisit) means keeping applications in the source environment because migration is blocked by compliance/regulatory constraints, technical dependencies, or lack of business justification (Application 2).

distractorNotes.a: Rehost involves migrating an application unchanged to AWS (lift and shift), which neither application will do.
distractorNotes.c: Refactor involves re-architecting applications to take advantage of cloud-native capabilities.
distractorNotes.e: Repurchase involves replacing custom applications with off-the-shelf SaaS products.

sourceNote: AWS Prescriptive Guidance - the 7 Rs migration strategies, retain and retire

stem: A geological survey team needs to transfer 120 TB of raw sensor data collected at a remote mountain research facility into Amazon S3. The facility connects to the internet over a slow, metered satellite uplink that would require over eighteen months to transmit the dataset over the network. Which AWS service should the team use to complete this data migration securely within a few days?

options.text: AWS Snowball Edge, using a ruggedized physical storage device to migrate petabyte-scale data offline
AWS Storage Gateway, deploying a local hybrid storage virtual appliance to cache data to Amazon S3
AWS Direct Connect, provisioning a dedicated private telecommunications circuit to bypass the satellite link
AWS DataSync, scheduling automated parallel network transfers over the existing satellite connection

explanation: AWS Snowball Edge is a physical data migration and edge computing device that comes in storage-optimized configurations (up to 80 TB or 210 TB usable storage). It is designed to move petabytes of data into and out of AWS securely when transferring data over the network is impractical due to limited bandwidth, high connectivity costs, or remote environments.

distractorNotes.b: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to cloud storage over existing network connections, which would remain bottlenecked by the slow satellite link.
distractorNotes.c: AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated physical telecommunications circuits between customer data centers and AWS, but cannot be provisioned to remote temporary mountain research sites.
distractorNotes.d: AWS DataSync accelerates data transfers over existing network links, but cannot overcome the physical throughput limitations of an 18-month satellite uplink.

sourceNote: AWS Snowball Developer Guide - What is AWS Snowball?

stem: A company’s Chief Financial Officer is preparing the financial transition plan for migrating on-premises workloads to AWS. In the on-premises model, the business purchased servers, storage arrays, and network switches every five years, depreciating these assets over their lifespan. In AWS, how does this expenditure structure fundamentally transform?

options.text: Operational expenses (OpEx) become capital expenses (CapEx), requiring multi-year upfront commitments to secure capacity
Capital expenses (CapEx) become operational expenses (OpEx), paying only for consumed resources as they are used
Capital expenses are retained by purchasing long-term server hardware leases directly from AWS financial services
Infrastructure depreciation is replaced by fixed monthly software subscription fees regardless of compute usage

explanation: Migrating to AWS represents a transition from Capital Expenditures (CapEx) to Operational Expenditures (OpEx). CapEx involves large upfront cash outlays to acquire physical assets that are capitalized and depreciated over several years. In contrast, cloud computing operates on an OpEx model where organizations pay only for the ongoing computing capacity they consume on a pay-as-you-go basis.

distractorNotes.a: Cloud computing shifts CapEx into OpEx, not OpEx into CapEx; furthermore, multi-year commitments are optional discount instruments rather than mandatory requirements.
distractorNotes.c: AWS does not lease physical server hardware to customers; computing resources are provisioned as on-demand utility services.
distractorNotes.d: AWS infrastructure services are billed on granular metered consumption rather than fixed monthly subscription fees that remain flat regardless of usage.

sourceNote: Six advantages of cloud computing - trade fixed expense for variable expense

stem: A company is conducting a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis to compare running a database on premises versus on Amazon RDS. When calculating the true cost of the on-premises environment, which operational and facility cost factors must be included beyond the purchase price of the database server hardware?

options.text: Direct capital server hardware depreciation and commercial hypervisor software maintenance license agreements
Application development contractor salaries, end-user desktop hardware, and corporate office real estate leases
Data center power, HVAC cooling, rack floor space, physical security, and ongoing server hardware maintenance
Third-party software quality assurance testing tools, business analytics consultants, and marketing platform retainers

explanation: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) encompasses all direct and indirect expenses associated with building and operating an environment. For on-premises data centers, TCO includes real estate floor space, power and electricity, cooling infrastructure (HVAC), physical security personnel, rack mounting, network hardware, server maintenance, spare parts, and labor for hardware operations.

distractorNotes.a: Considering only direct server hardware depreciation and hypervisor licensing severely undercounts on-premises TCO by ignoring continuous power, cooling, facility space, and hardware maintenance overhead.
distractorNotes.b: Application software contractor salaries and corporate end-user office leases exist regardless of where workloads run and are not part of data center infrastructure facility TCO.
distractorNotes.d: Quality assurance tooling and marketing consulting retainers are business operating expenses unrelated to on-premises server infrastructure and facility TCO.

sourceNote: Migration Hub User Guide - Migration Evaluator and TCO assessment factors

stem: An enterprise holds existing perpetual Microsoft SQL Server and Windows Server software licenses with active Software Assurance from its on-premises environment. When migrating these workloads to Amazon EC2, the company wants to continue using its existing licenses rather than paying AWS for newly bundled licenses in the hourly instance rate. Which cloud licensing approach fulfills this requirement?

options.text: License Included, bundling all third-party operating system and database software licenses into the hourly compute rate
AWS Marketplace private offers, purchasing custom enterprise software subscriptions directly through vendor contracts
Enterprise Discount Program (EDP), converting on-premises perpetual software licenses into pooled AWS usage credits
Bring Your Own License (BYOL), allowing customers to utilize existing eligible enterprise software licenses on AWS

explanation: Bring Your Own License (BYOL) is a licensing model that allows customers to migrate existing eligible enterprise software licenses (such as Microsoft Windows Server, SQL Server, or Oracle) to AWS (such as on Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts or supported EC2 instances), utilizing their existing software investments and avoiding recurring license fees bundled by AWS.

distractorNotes.a: License Included is the model where AWS provides the software license as part of the hourly compute rate, which would duplicate the company's existing licenses.
distractorNotes.b: AWS Marketplace private offers enable procurement of new software subscriptions and negotiated pricing from independent software vendors, rather than reusing existing perpetual licenses.
distractorNotes.c: The Enterprise Discount Program provides tiered discounts based on overall AWS spending commitments, but does not convert external software licenses into AWS usage credits.

sourceNote: AWS License Manager User Guide - Bring Your Own License (BYOL) overview

stem: A company migrated a suite of internal applications from on-premises physical servers to Amazon EC2 instances by matching the exact CPU and memory specifications of the old hardware. After three months of operations, AWS Cost Explorer reports that the instances consistently average under 8% CPU utilization and 15% memory usage. What cost optimization practice should the company perform first before purchasing commitment discounts?

options.text: Rightsizing, modifying instance types and sizes to match actual workload performance and resource demands
Purchasing 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the existing instance fleet to lock in maximum discounts
Deploying instances into an additional Availability Zone to distribute the idle compute load geographically
Converting the instances to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to ensure continuous uninterrupted processing capacity

explanation: Rightsizing is the process of matching instance types and sizes to actual workload performance and capacity requirements at the lowest possible cost. AWS best practices mandate rightsizing overprovisioned instances first before purchasing commitment-based pricing options (such as Savings Plans or Reserved Instances) so that you do not commit to paying for oversized capacity.

distractorNotes.b: Purchasing Reserved Instances for oversized instances locks the organization into paying for unneeded capacity for multiple years.
distractorNotes.c: Adding another Availability Zone increases infrastructure redundancy and cost, but does not solve resource overprovisioning.
distractorNotes.d: Spot Instances can be interrupted with two minutes' notice when AWS needs the capacity back, and using Spot does not eliminate the fundamental waste of oversized resource configurations.

sourceNote: Cost Management User Guide - Rightsizing recommendations in Cost Explorer

stem: According to the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF), cloud transformation enables organizations to achieve measurable business outcomes beyond basic infrastructure modernization. Which TWO of the following are recognized AWS CAF business outcomes? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Elimination of all technical debt by replacing custom applications with fully managed SaaS offerings
Transfer of enterprise regulatory compliance accountability and audit liability entirely to AWS
Reduced business risk, improving security posture, operational resilience, and compliance
Conversion of all cloud operating expenses into capitalized assets depreciated across multiple years
Increased operational efficiency, lowering unit costs and automating routine operational tasks

explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) identifies four core business outcomes driven by cloud transformation: (1) Reduced business risk (improving security, resilience, and compliance), (2) Increased operational efficiency (lowering unit costs and improving productivity), (3) Accelerated business agility and revenue growth, and (4) Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance improvement.

distractorNotes.a: Migrating to the cloud or adopting SaaS does not automatically eliminate technical debt or architecture maintenance.
distractorNotes.b: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, customers remain fully accountable and liable for their own regulatory compliance posture and audits.
distractorNotes.d: Cloud computing operates on a pay-as-you-go operational expenditure (OpEx) model, not capitalizing infrastructure into multi-year depreciable assets.

sourceNote: AWS CAF - Cloud acceleration outcomes and business benefits
